newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Green light for international force to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Green light for international force to Zaire.

text.p: A scaled-down international force has been given the green light to assist refugees in eastern Zaire as Rwandan-backed rebels extend their control over much of the troubled region.

"Now the multinational force is formally constituted," Canadian Assistant Deputy Foreign Minister Paul Heinbecker told reporters in Ottawa on Friday after chairing a meeting of ambassadors from 14 countries.

More than 20 countries, including the United States, France, Britain, Belgium, Senegal and South Africa, will contribute to the Canadian-led mission, which is likely to comprise 1,000 or 2,000 troops instead of the 10,000 originally planned.

The green light came nearly three weeks after Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien began urging world leaders to rescue what aid agencies said at the time were more than a million refugees and displaced people in strife-torn eastern Zaire.

Since then about 600,000 refugees have returned to Rwanda. Heinbecker said at least 140,000 more had been identified in Zaire, and western officials have said there could be hundreds of thousands of others as well as displaced Zaireans.
Friday's meeting approved a Canadian proposal to set up a multinational military headquarters in the Ugandan capital Entebbe, pursue reconnaissance missions and prepare for possible airdrops.

Ideally, aid would be delivered through truck convoys rather than dropped from the air, Canadian officials said. "If the permission is given for the convoys to drive in, they'll go in," said Heinbecker.
It will now be up to the force's commander, Canadian Lieutenant General Maurice Baril, to piece together exactly what the mission requires and what each country will do.
A top priority would be to step up reconnaissance in eastern Zaire to identify people in need before any airdrops could be undertaken.

Zairean Information Minister Boguo Makeli said Zaire would not allow overflights for airdrops, but Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said Canada had obtained the full approval of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.
U.N. sources said on Friday rebels had strengthened their position in eastern Zaire, capturing Butembo and fighting the Zairean army near other towns.
The sources said a Butembo resident, contacted by radio, reported rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for Liberation of Congo-Zaire had entered the town on Thursday.

The U.N. sources said fighting was taking place further north near the towns of Beni and Bunia, ADFL rebels now control a large swathe of eastern Zaire with the cities of Uvira, Kamanyola, Bukavu and Goma firmly under their control.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila has repeatedly said his forces would fight all the way to the capital Kinshasa to topple the ailing Mobutu.
Zaire, aid workers and diplomats say Kabila's group is backed by Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army, a charge Rwanda denies.
The go-ahead for the international force came as refugees continued to flow back across the border to Rwanda.

A spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said more than 7,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees had returned home on Friday and some 40,000 were heading for the eastern Zairean town of Sake, near the border, from nearby Minova.
In Bukavu, further south, UNHCR officials said 1,500 refugees crossed from Zaire on Friday.
Aid officials say they are not allowed to travel far beyond Bukavu, severely hampering efforts to help thousands of refugees who may still be hiding in the forests of eastern Zaire.

Refugees arriving in Bukavu on Friday said former Rwandan army troops and Interahamwe militiamen had threatened to kill those who tried to go home, but hunger and cold in the forests had forced them out.
Some aid officials have said privately they believe refugees still in Zaire could be the Interahamwe, former Rwandan army troops and their families.
The Interahamwe and their former army allies were the chief culprits of the 1994 genocide in Rwanda in which up to one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed. REUTER
